The simplest way is to declare `examples` on your Pydantic model using `model_config`. That extra info will be added as-is to the output **JSON Schema** for that model, and it will be used in the API docs.[5]

```python
class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None
    price: float
    tax: float | None = None

    model_config = {
        "json_schema_extra": {
            "examples": [
                {
                    "name": "Foo",
                    "description": "A very nice Item",
                    "price": 35.4,
                    "tax": 3.2,
                }
            ]
        }
    }
```

**Other options:**

- **Per field:** When using `Field()` with Pydantic models, you can also declare additional `examples`[2], e.g. `name: str = Field(examples=["Foo"])`.
- **In the endpoint:** Pass `examples` to `Body()`:

```python
item: Annotated[
    Item,
    Body(examples=[{"name": "Foo", "description": "A very nice Item", "price": 35.4, "tax": 3.2}]),
]
```

**Caveats:**

- If you pass multiple examples, Swagger UI, the tool in charge of showing the docs UI, doesn't support showing multiple examples for the data in **JSON Schema**.[1] The docs mention a workaround using `openapi_examples` in `Body()`. These excerpts don't include the full code for it, so check the "OpenAPI-specific examples" section of the [Declare Request Example Data](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/schema-extra-example/) page.
- Use `examples` (a list) instead of the old `example` keyword. The old keyword is still supported by OpenAPI 3.1.0, but is deprecated and is not part of the JSON Schema standard.[5]
